                                           On the non-existence of finite groups with certain normal subgroups
                                                                                             Ihechukwu Chinyere∗

                                          Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematics, University of Pretoria, Hatfield 0028,
                                                                         Pretoria, South Africa

                                                                                               January 6, 2026


                                                                                                    Abstract
arXiv:2601.01080v1 [math.GR] 3 Jan 2026




                                                    Problem 20.21 of Mazurov and Khukhro (Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook,
                                                 20th Issue, 2022), contributed by M. Conder and attributed to G. Verret, asks whether there exists a finite
                                                 group G with two normal subgroups K and L of index 12 such that K ∼         = L, but with non-isomorphic
                                                 quotients G/K ∼ = C12 and G/L ∼ = A4 . We prove that no such finite group exists.


                                          1      Introduction
                                          Understanding the relationships between normal subgroups and their quotients is a central topic in finite group
                                          theory, as it provides deep insight into the structure and composition of groups. The study of such subgroups
                                          reveals intricate constraints on how a group can be assembled from simpler pieces. Problem 20.21 of Mazurov
                                          and Khukhro [1] (Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 20th Issue, 2022), contributed
                                          by M. Conder and attributed to G. Verret, asks whether there exists a finite group G with two normal subgroups
                                          K and L, each of index 12 in G, such that K ∼   = L, but

                                                                                     G/K ∼
                                                                                         = C12        while    G/L ∼
                                                                                                                   = A4 .

                                          Our main result gives a definitive negative answer:

                                          Theorem 1. There does not exist a finite group G with normal subgroups K and L such that both K and L
                                          have index 12, are isomorphic, G/K ∼
                                                                             = C12 , and G/L ∼
                                                                                             = A4 .

                                          This theorem demonstrates that the presence of isomorphic normal subgroups of equal index places strong
                                          constraints on the resulting quotient groups, excluding certain combinations even when the indices coincide.


                                          2      Preliminaries
                                          Throughout, all groups are finite. Suppose there exists a finite group G with normal subgroups K, L◁G satisfying

                                                                  [G : K] = [G : L] = 12,         G/K ∼
                                                                                                      = C12 ,       G/L ∼
                                                                                                                        = A4 ,     K∼
                                                                                                                                    = L.

                                          These conditions imply that K and hence L are nontrivial subgroups of G. Let

                                                                                     n := |K| = |L|,          H := K ∩ L.

                                          Since intersections of normal subgroups are normal, we have H ◁ G. Let f : K → L be an isomorphism, set

                                                                                             X := H ∩ f (H) ≤ H.

                                          Notation: Cn is the cyclic group of order n, A4 is the alternating group of order 12, V4 is the Klein four-group,
                                          D2n the dihedral group of order 2n, Q12 the dicyclic group of order 12, and Q8 the quaternion group of order 8.
                                          We include the following well-known result for easy reference:
                                              ∗ Corresponding author: i.chinyere@up.ac.za;   ihechukwu@aims.ac.za


                                                                                                        1
Lemma 2. With the above notation, the following hold:

    1. K̄ := K/H and L̄ := L/H are normal in Ḡ := G/H with trivial intersection K̄ ∩ L̄.
    2. The natural quotient maps πK : Ḡ ↠ G/K and πL : Ḡ ↠ G/L have kernels K̄ and L̄, so that Ḡ/K̄ ∼
                                                                                                       = G/K
       and Ḡ/L̄ ∼
                 = G/L.
    3. The product KL is normal in G, with order |KL| = |K||L|/|H| = n2 /|H|.

It follows from Lemma 2 that K̄ naturally embeds in Ḡ/L̄ ∼= G/L ∼ = A4 and L̄ naturally embeds in Ḡ/K̄ ∼  =
       ∼
G/K = C12 . We will use this fact throughout, and all subsequent references to embeddings of K̄ or L̄ refer to
these canonical embeddings.

Lemma 3. Given the above notations, H/X and f (H)/X are normal subgroups of L/X.

Proof. First, we show that f (H) is normal in L. Since f is an isomorphism from K to L and H ◁ K, for any
ℓ ∈ L = f (K) there exists k ∈ K such that f (k) = ℓ. For any h ∈ H, we have

                               ℓf (h)ℓ−1 = f (k)f (h)f (k)−1 = f (khk −1 ) ∈ f (H),

because khk −1 ∈ H as H ◁ K. Therefore, f (H) is closed under conjugation by all elements of L, so f (H) ◁ L.
Next, define X := H ∩ f (H). Since both H and f (H) are normal in L, their intersection X is also normal in L.
Finally, consider the quotients H/X and f (H)/X inside L/X. It is a standard fact that if N ◁ G and M ◁ G
with M ⊆ N , then N/M ◁ G/M . Applying this to H and f (H) with M = X ◁ L, we conclude that H/X ◁ L/X
and f (H)/X ◁ L/X.


3     Proof of Theorem 1
Suppose, for contradiction, that a finite group G satisfying the hypotheses exists.

3.1       Reduction modulo H
Consider the quotient Ḡ := G/H with normal subgroups K̄ := K/H and L̄ := L/H. We have K̄ ◁ Ḡ and
L̄ ◁ Ḡ with trivial intersection K̄ ∩ L̄ = 1. Moreover, K̄ ,→ G/L ∼= A4 and L̄ ,→ G/K ∼ = C12 . By Lemma 2,
K̄ is isomorphic to a normal subgroup of A4 ; hence its possible orders are determined by the normal subgroup
structure of A4 . Hence,
                                                                        n n no
                               |K̄| ∈ {1, 4, 12} =⇒     |H| = |K|/|K̄| ∈ n, ,      .
                                                                            4 12
If |K̄| = n, then H = 1, so that K ∼
                                   = K/H ∼  = L/f (H) ∼
                                                      = L. But this leads to a contradiction: K/H ◁ G/L ∼
                                                                                                        = A4 ,
whereas L/H ◁ G/K ∼  = C12 . There is no way for a nontrivial group to be normal simultaneously in A4 and C12 ,
so this case cannot occur. Hence,
                                                                  nn n o
                                    |K̄| ∈ {4, 12}  =⇒      |H| ∈     ,    .
                                                                    4 12

3.2       Possible sizes of X
Recall that
                                             X := H ∩ f (H) ≤ H,
where f : K → L is an isomorphism. By the subgroup product formula,

                              |X||Hf (H)| = |H| |f (H)| = |H|2 ≤ |L||X| = n|X|,

so that
                                                     |H|2
                                                  |X| ≥   .
                                                       n
Moreover, since X ≤ H, the order of X must divide |H|, so we can write l|X| = |H| for some integer l ≥ 1.
Combining these constraints gives

                            |H|2 ≤ |X|n ≤ |H|n,       |X|l = |H| for some integer l.

Depending on the value of |H|, we distinguish two main cases:


                                                        2
   1. |H| = n/4, then
                                                          n n n n no
                                                  |X| =      ∈   , ,  .
                                                          4l   16 8 4
   2. |H| = n/12, then
                                    n    n n   n   n   n n n n n n n n no
                           |X| =       ∈     ,   ,   ,   , , , , , , , ,          .
                                   12l    144 132 120 108 96 84 72 60 48 36 24 12
This gives the complete set of possible orders of X, taking into account both the subgroup product inequality
and the divisibility constraint from X ≤ H.
Depending on the value of |X|, we distinguish two main possibilities. Either X is a proper, possibly trivial,
subgroup of H, so that 1 ≤ |X| < |H|, or X coincides with H, that is, |X| = |H|.

3.3    Case |X| = |H|
If |H| = n/4, then |K/H| = |L/H| = 4. Since K̄ = K/H embeds into G/L ∼       = A4 and L̄ = L/H embeds into
      ∼                                             ∼
G/K = C12 , we would need an isomorphism K/H = L/H. However, this is impossible: the only subgroup of
order 4 in A4 is the Klein four-group V4 , whereas the only subgroup of order 4 in C12 is cyclic C4 . Therefore,
no isomorphism exists between K̄ and L̄ in this case.
If |H| = n/12, then |K/H| = |L/H| = 12. The groups of order 12 are

                                            C12 , C6 × C2 , A4 , D12 , Q12 .

The embeddings K̄ = K/H ,→ G/L ∼    = A4 and L̄ = L/H ,→ G/K ∼   = C12 impose strong restrictions: K/H must
be isomorphic to a subgroup of A4 of order 12, and L/H to a subgroup of C12 of order 12. Hence K/H ∼      = A4
and L/H ∼= C12 . However, this is impossible, since A4 ∼
                                                       ̸ C12 . Therefore, no group of order 12 can satisfy both
                                                        =
embedding requirements, yielding a contradiction.

3.4    Case 1 ≤ |X| < |H|
By Lemma 3, both H/X and f (H)/X are normal in L/X. Set

                            L1 := L/X,        H1 := H/X ◁ L1 ,       H2 := f (H)/X ◁ L1 .

Since f : K → L is an isomorphism and H ◁ K, the first isomorphism theorem gives K/H ∼
                                                                                     = L/f (H), and the
Third Isomorphism Theorem yields

                                   L1 /H1 ∼
                                          = L/H    and    L1 /H2 ∼
                                                                 = L/f (H) ∼
                                                                           = K/H.

From previous reductions, L/H ∼
                              = C4 and K/H ∼
                                           = V4 , so

                                          L1 /H1 ∼
                                                 = C4     and   L1 /H2 ∼
                                                                       = V4 .

Thus, L1 contains two distinct normal subgroups H1 , H2 of equal order with non-isomorphic quotients. The
orders of L1 and H1 are
                                |L1 | = |L|/|X| = n/|X|,   |H1 | = |H|/|X|,
giving the finite list of possibilities displayed in Table 1.

        |H|                            |L1 |                                             |H1 |
       n/4                          4, 8, 16                                            1, 2, 4
       n/12    12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120, 132, 144     3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36

                             Table 1: Possible orders of L1 and H1 to check in GAP.

The GAP computation in Appendix A exhaustively checks all groups of these orders and confirms that none
admits two distinct normal subgroups of equal order, non-characteristic, with quotients C4 and V4 . Consequently,
no group L1 arises in this manner, and therefore no finite group G satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 1.

                                               4
A     GAP Computation
Exhaustively examines all groups of the orders listed in Table 1 and verifies that none admits two distinct normal
subgroups H1 , H2 of equal order such that neither H1 nor H2 is characteristic in L1 with quotients C4 and V4 .

CheckGroups:= function()
    local IsCharacteristic, Listn, n, groups, L_1, found, Hc4, Hv4, h1, h2, foundPair;
    #Test whether a subgroup is characteristic
    IsCharacteristic:= function(G, H)
        local A, a;
        A:= AutomorphismGroup(G);
        for a in GeneratorsOfGroup(A) do
            if Image(a, H) <> H then
                return false;
            fi;
        od;
        return true;
    end;
    #Relevant orders of L_1 to check
    Listn := [4,8,12,16,24,36,48,60,72,84,96,108,120,132,144];
    for n in Listn do
        Print("\n=== Groups of order ", n, " ===\n");
        groups:= AllSmallGroups(n);
        found:= false;
        for L_1 in groups do
            #Normal subgroups H_1 with quotient C4
            Hc4:= Filtered(NormalSubgroups(L_1),
                            h -> StructureDescription(L_1/h) = "C4"
                                 and not IsCharacteristic(L_1,h));
            #Normal subgroups H_2 with quotient V4
            Hv4:= Filtered(NormalSubgroups(L_1),
                            h -> StructureDescription(L_1/h) = "V4"
                                 and not IsCharacteristic(L_1,h));
            #Check for two distinct subgroups
            foundPair := false;
            for h1 in Hc4 do
                for h2 in Hv4 do
                    if h1 <> h2 then
                        foundPair := true;
                    fi;
                od;
            od;
            if foundPair then
                found:= true;
                Print("FOUND in L_1 = ", IdGroup(L_1), " : ",
                      StructureDescription(L_1), "\n");
                Print("|L_1| = ", Order(L_1), "\n");
                Print("Distinct normal non-char subgps H_1, H_2 give quotients C4 and V4\n");
            fi;
        od;
        if not found then
            Print("No group of order ", n,
                  "admits distinct normal non-char subgps H_1, H_2 with quotients C4 and V4.\n");
        fi;
    od;
end;
CheckGroups();
